exec.thesis: Lighter pairs the sector's cleanest value-accrual design — 100% of trading fees fund open-market buybacks, now permanently burned — with a business whose revenue has halved every quarter since TGE (Q4 '25 $39.7M → Q1 $19.7M → Q2 $9.6M) as points-farming volume unwound. At $2.45 ($2.45B FDV) it trades ~60x run-rate fees: Hyperliquid's multiple without Hyperliquid's organic flow, meaning the price already pays for a Robinhood-driven re-acceleration that hasn't shown up in the fee data yet. The float story cuts both ways — burns retired 6.3% of circulating supply, but the Dec 29 '26 team/investor cliff opens ~13.9M LIT/month (~$34M) of new supply for 36 months against ~$56M/day of spot volume and a ±2% book of only ~$1.5M.
own: Most direct value accrual in the sector: 100% of trading fees → buyback-and-burn, ~5.1% annualized yield on market cap at current run-rate, plus ~6% staking with 50% of float already staked.
Robinhood is both an investor and a launch partner: Robinhood Chain integration (Jul 1 '26, $11M LIT committed, 2x points) is a real consumer-distribution option no perp-DEX peer has.
The tech is real and hard to replicate: SNARK-verified order book (matching, margin, liquidations all proved), ex-Citadel/Jump team, $90M from Founders Fund/Ribbit/Haun at $1.5B.
avoid: Fundamentals still falling: protocol revenue halved each quarter post-airdrop; blended take rate ~0.77bps is ~10x thinner than Hyperliquid per dollar of volume; 30d volume is −82% from the Dec '25 peak.
Supply wall: from Dec 29 '26, ~1.4% of supply unlocks monthly for 36 months (~$34M/mo at current price) into ~$1.5M of ±2% book depth — buyback firepower ($2.5M/mo and shrinking) can't absorb it.
Priced for the turnaround: ~60x declining run-rate fees, plus single-sequencer operational risk (4.5h outage during the Oct 10 '25 cascade, LLP −5.35%).
questions: Does Robinhood Chain distribution convert into measurable non-incentive volume by Q4 '26?
Can the 250M ecosystem pool fund ~6% staking yield without depleting, now that it (not revenue) pays stakers?
Does the estimated ~$40M/yr Circle USDC float income ever get formally pledged to the token? That would roughly double token-directed cash flow overnight.

biz.narrative: Lighter is a ZK-rollup order-book perp DEX: free for retail, paid for professionals. Standard accounts pay 0/0 maker-taker (with deliberate 200–300ms latency); opt-in Premium accounts (MMs, HFT, API) pay 0.004%/0.028% with lower latency, discountable up to 30% by staking LIT. Blended take rate is ~0.77bps of volume — roughly 10x thinner than Hyperliquid. 100% of trading-fee revenue funds daily TWAP buybacks of LIT (burned since Jul '26). Separately, a Feb '26 Circle deal shares yield on ~$920M of platform USDC (~$40M/yr est.) — that float income accrues to the company, not the token, and doesn't appear in DeFiLlama fee lines. Liquidation fees route to the LLP liquidity pool. Team is lean (~16–18 FTE), so operating leverage is extreme in both directions: fees fell with farming volume, and would flow straight to buybacks if volume returns.
notes: Volume quality improving: volume/OI ratio now ~1.7x vs ~8x during points farming — but 30d volume ($43B) is still −82% from the Dec '25 peak ($232B).
Monthly fee split within quarters is estimated from DeFiLlama quarterly income statements (Q4 $39.7M → Q1 $19.7M → Q2 $9.6M) — trend is hard data, monthly shape is interpolated.
No public wallet-level concentration data for MM share of volume — flagged gap; the bifurcated fee model means revenue depends heavily on the Premium/API cohort.
Circle float income (~$40M/yr est.) rivals all trading fees combined — the single biggest unpriced lever if ever pledged to the token.

moat.note: Tech/IP is the standout: SNARK-verified matching is genuinely differentiated and durable ~18–24mo. Liquidity network effects are real but far behind Hyperliquid (which is re-concentrating share, ~37–44% of perp-DEX volume). Regulatory is thinnest — US-regulated perps (Kalshi BTCPERP approved May '26, Coinbase, CME lawsuit pending) are a live substitution vector.

liquidity.summary: Aggregate ±2% book depth is only ~$1.3M ask / ~$1.6M bid across all venues, against ~$56M spot ADV (plus ~$120M+ CEX-perp notional) — thin absolute depth typical of a 25%-float token. Blocks above ~$2M need TWAP or perp-hedged execution; above ~$10M you exhaust visible books. Deepest −2% books: Coinbase and Lighter's own DEX; tightest spreads: Bybit/OKX.

tech.narrative: zkLighter is an app-specific ZK-rollup settling to Ethereum with a verifiable order book: SNARK proofs cover not just state transitions but the exchange logic itself — price-time priority matching, margin checks, and liquidations are all cryptographically proved. This is the genuine differentiator vs. both Hyperliquid (own L1, trust-the-validators) and CEXs (trust-the-operator). Latency is deliberately tiered as a product (140–300ms by account class) on a ms-level engine. The embedded bull-case assumption: verifiability + execution quality wins institutional flow as perps legitimize. The embedded risk: it all runs on a single centralized sequencer today — the Oct 10 '25 cascade caused a 4.5-hour outage (index corruption under load, LLP −5.35%, 2,000+ users compensated).

devs.title: Sequencer decentralization
devs.body: The proven single point of failure. Verifiable matching makes decentralization architecturally tractable, but execution is unproven — this is the gating item for the institutional thesis.

devs.title: RWA / equity / FX perps + prediction markets
devs.body: Chainlink-oracle RWA perps live (premium fees since Apr '26); pre-IPO markets, prediction markets, and collateral expansion (tokenized gold, BTC, equities as margin) slated Q3 '26. Expands TAM beyond crypto-native perps.

devs.title: US-regulated perpetuals
devs.body: Kalshi's BTCPERP approved by CFTC May 29 '26 (first US-regulated true perp); Coinbase routing global perps via Bermuda; CME sued the CFTC same day. Substitution threat for US flow — but legal legitimization is also a sector tailwind.

devs.title: Robinhood Chain consumer distribution
devs.body: Robinhood Wallet users can post collateral directly into Lighter perps (2x points, $11M LIT committed). Tests whether distribution can beat liquidity-depth moats — the single most watchable Lighter-specific development.

catalysts.mid: The 12–36mo re-rating rests on three legs: (1) durable non-incentive volume — Robinhood consumer flow plus RWA/equity perps replacing the departed points farmers; (2) the Circle float income (~$40M/yr est., currently at the opco) being formally pledged to the token, which would roughly double token-directed cash flow and re-frame LIT as the sector's yield asset; (3) sector legal clarity from the CME-v-CFTC fight — legitimized perps grow the pie but also arm CEX/TradFi substitutes. Compression scenario: Hyperliquid's re-concentration (37–44% share and rising) plus zero-fee competition makes take-rate expansion impossible, and LIT's multiple converges down toward shrinking fees.

variant: Consensus reads the burn + Robinhood news as the turnaround and is paying ~60x for it. The variant is structural: Lighter's buyback is revenue-funded, so it's pro-cyclical — firepower shrinks exactly when volume (and price) fall, and the Dec '26 cliff arrives with the buyback near cycle lows. That makes the 'structural bid' thesis weaker than it looks on paper. The defensible non-consensus long isn't the burn — it's the unpriced Circle float income (~$40M/yr, invisible in DeFiLlama, roughly equal to ALL trading fees). A formal pledge of float economics to the token is the single event that would change the math overnight; watch team communications for it.

valuation.embedded: Reverse-engineered: at $2.45 the market pays ~60x a fee base that halved two quarters running. To earn a market return at a 25x exit multiple, fees must roughly triple to ~$120M/yr by 2029 — i.e., the price embeds substantial Robinhood/RWA success, or early credit for Circle float economics reaching the token. Note LIT trades at rough multiple parity with Hyperliquid on run-rate fees despite inferior flow quality — the market is already paying the 'quality tech + Robinhood' premium.

synthesis: Lighter pairs the sector's most shareholder-like token design with post-airdrop fundamentals that are still finding a floor. The tech is real, the burn is real, and Robinhood is a distribution option nobody else has — but at ~60x declining run-rate fees the market has already paid for the turnaround, while a 36-month, ~$400M/yr supply spigot opens in five months against a $1.5M ±2% order book. The asymmetry today is poor for size; it turns attractive either materially lower (into cliff fear — both prior sector cliff patterns and LIT's own post-airdrop capitulation were the buying moments) or on hard evidence of organic volume inflection.
recText: Recommendation: watchlist, not a core position today. Tactical only around catalyst windows (burns, Robinhood milestones) with tight stops given 7%+ daily vol. Structural entry target: the Dec '26–Q1 '27 cliff window, or sub-$1.50 with fees stabilizing. Priority follow-ups: non-incentive volume forensics (Dune wallet cohorts), and any signal that Circle float economics get pledged to LIT.
